harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo invocation (user, timestamp, host, command) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in, while disabling sudo's syslog output so entries no longer land in /var/log/secure (the general system log). Verified functionality before and after a full node restart, confirming persistence.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: sudo previously logged via authpriv syslog facility into /var/log/secure, no prior sudoers.d customization existed

Created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logfile with 'Defaults !syslog' (disables syslog logging per sudoers manual), 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"', and 'Defaults log_host, log_year, log_input, log_output'
Validated syntax with visudo -c, set file mode 440
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log owned root:root, mode 600

Created a temporary non-root sudo-capable test user (sudologtest) to verify per-user attribution, ran sudo commands as that user, confirmed entries appeared in the new log with user/timestamp/host while /var/log/secure line count stayed flat, then removed the test user, its sudoers rule, and cleared the test log entries
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, sudoers.d file contents, visudo validation, log file permissions
Restarted node1 via 'systemctl reboot' launched with a delayed background wrapper so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, observing a connection timeout during the outage window
Verified changed boot_id (f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892 -> 2cdef81a-e59d-4bf7-bb37-a735057f1ec9) and new uptime-since, proving an actual restart occurred

Re-verified post-restart: sudoers.d config intact and valid, log file intact, ran a fresh sudo command and confirmed it landed in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp/host while /var/log/secure line count was unchanged before/after

evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: sudoers.d/sudo-logfile created and validated with visudo -c; log file created with 600 perms; test sudo commands by root and a test user recorded with timestamp, host, user, and command in /var/log/sudo-commands.log

evidence.requirement: sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo previously wrote to /var/log/secure via authpriv syslog; after adding 'Defaults !syslog', /var/log/secure line count stayed identical (14->14, and 34->34 post-reboot) across sudo invocations, proving no new general-log entries were produced
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime, sudoers.d config contents, visudo validation, and log file permissions as the healthy baseline

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled via a detached background wrapper; command acknowledged successfully before the node went offline

evidence.requirement: proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while node1 was rebooting; exec became available again shortly after; boot_id changed from f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892 to 2cdef81a-e59d-4bf7-bb37-a735057f1ec9, with a fresh uptime-since timestamp, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and data
evidence.summary: After restart, sudoers.d/sudo-logfile persisted and revalidated with visudo -c, log file permissions intact, and a fresh sudo command was correctly captured in /var/log/sudo-commands.log while /var/log/secure remained unaffected

Verified functionality before and after a full node restart, confirming persistence.
